rule.states: commands run in zsh; quote a pattern meant for a program and a word that begins with =, and a pattern left for zsh must match a file; write the name in braces before a colon or a bracket; a parameter is one word; never assign path or status; backquotes run in double quotes; scripts go in files by a quoted heredoc; the host has no gawk, timeout or tac

mechanism.classifier: packages/skeleton/src/harness-command.ts: shellDiagnostics and shellGuidance, with a reader of the command's words written for them; no existing export or judgment changes, and the tokenizer the guards use is not called
mechanism.reader: Bounded static reading of parsed executable, argument, assignment, redirection and case-pattern roles, active quotes/control syntax, command and process substitutions, heredocs, and literal scripts handed to a shell or eval. Quoted executable names remain executable; printed text and comments do not supply executable roles. Literal preceding assignments can corroborate a parameter command head within its scope; temporary prefix assignments and isolated shell scopes do not supply that binding. Reads the first 262144 characters; arbitrary dynamic shell semantics are not executed or fully evaluated.
mechanism.line: A line counts when it opens with the shell's name as the host runs it or as an inner zsh prints it, the name of a builtin that refused where there is one, and a line number; a line longer than 4,096 characters is passed over and sixteen findings end the reading.
mechanism.observer: packages/skeleton/src/harness-host.ts: observeShellDiagnostics, called last in the observe branch after every call, so a call whose other observations fail is neither counted nor answered; an error inside it changes nothing else, and a count that cannot be written does not stop the answer to the call's own command
mechanism.failedCommand: The host runs no registered hook for a result it marks failed. At each observed call the observer reads the last 262,144 bytes of the agent's own transcript, a subagent's in its own file under the session's directory, and answers each failed shell result once, the last four at most. The row it writes holds the mark and the SHA-256 of the host's call identifier; a failed result whose row cannot be written is not answered, since the row is what keeps the answer from being repeated. Answer identities are read across the intact lane in 65536-byte buffers with at most a 4096-character carried line, retaining only the eligible at-most-four hashes and stopping when all are found. Ordinary lane growth never ages an eligible identity out; duplicate result parts count once. Lane IO can grow with the distance to eligible rows; no second cache or lane is created. Concurrent observers claim an eligible use by atomic placement of an ignored directory named by its hash, containing an immutable nonce-named record of the short-lived hook process. They recheck the intact lane under that claim before appending or answering. Completion or write failure releases the claim; a dead owner is recovered only by removing its exact nonce, so a delayed reclaimer cannot delete a live replacement. No waiter sleeps. Malformed or unreadable claim records are left untouched and supply no answer at that call.
mechanism.answer: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext for PostToolUse: each sentence once and whole within 900 characters for the call's own command, and within 900 more for each of at most four earlier failed commands, opened by words that say so (WO-172-D060). It holds what the command itself wrote, except that a builtin's bad-option subject is taken from the printed line, whole or not at all at 120 characters, without control or format characters. No decision, no block, no terminal message, and nothing at all when no diagnostic is found.

classes.unmatched-pattern: an unquoted word of the command becomes the pattern the shell named once zsh has changed its parameters, its leading tilde and its braces; answered by form: an option's value or the word after a pattern flag with the quoted form, a file operand with both readings, a substitution inside an unquoted heredoc with the delimiter to quote
classes.bad-pattern: an unquoted word becomes the pattern named; or, for the messages zsh gives when it reads parentheses as qualifiers of a file pattern, an unquoted word holds an opening parenthesis after a character
classes.equals-word: an unquoted word holds an equals sign at its start, or after an equals sign or a colon, followed by the rest the shell named, to the word's end
classes.program-not-found: A parsed executable head names the program, either literally or through a preceding standalone literal assignment in its scope; arguments, comments, printed phrases and temporary prefix assignments cannot supply the executable role.
classes.unsplit-word: the shell named a program or a file whose name holds a blank or a line break, no word of the command becomes that path, and a parameter stands as a whole word
classes.reserved-parameter: the command assigns the parameter named: as an assignment, or as the name a loop, a read or a declaration sets
classes.bad-substitution: outside single quotes the command holds a colon and a letter after a parameter, a form of bash, or a braced expansion
classes.bad-subscript: outside single quotes the command holds a bracket after a parameter
classes.bad-math: outside single quotes the command holds an arithmetic form or a bracket after a parameter
classes.bash-parameter: the shell named one of bash's own parameters as not set and the command holds it outside single quotes
classes.builtin-option: the line carries a builtin's name, the command runs that builtin and holds the option named
classes.unmatched-quote: An unclosed active quote, including a saved outer quote around an unfinished substitution, matches the named quote; balanced printed quote characters are inert.
classes.parse-error: Active malformed control/operator syntax, an unmatched closer, or an unfinished construct corroborates the named token/span or end of input; valid elif branches and case-arm pattern closers do not corroborate printed errors.
classes.missing-file: An executable or redirection path becomes the name, or an operand of the builtin that actually ran becomes its named path; unrelated printed arguments do not supply that role.
classes.not-permitted: The appropriate executable, redirection or executed-builtin operand becomes the path; for a refused background-job priority, the command starts a background job.
classes.other: An unlisted initial diagnostic counts only when a named tilde expansion or the executed builtin corroborates it; it supplies no guidance.

lane.session: the SHA-256 of the session identifier, as the journals are named
neverHolds: a raw session or tool identifier
a field a guard's count reads
lane.lifetime: removed with the worktree, as the gate index is; a planning pass on main sees main's rows
lane.marked: failed, on a row for a command whose result the host marked failed
lane.use: the SHA-256 of the host's identifier of that call
lane.writtenThrough: its own entry, opened without following a link; a link in its place, to a file or to nothing, loses the count and writes nothing

A command that holds several classes is counted once in each. A session or a thread is counted when it holds a line before the cutoff. A failed result is read as the observer reads one, without the status the host opens it with. A Codex call that is a script handing commands to its tool is read for the commands it carries. Whether the host marked a result failed is the host's own mark.

limits: The answer to a command whose result the host marked failed arrives at the next observed call, not at the failed call. It does not arrive when no further call is observed, when the result has left the last 262,144 bytes of the transcript, or for more than the last four failed results between two observed calls.

A word-splitting mistake leaves a diagnostic only where the whole value names a program or a file. Where a program receives the value as one argument the shell says nothing, so neither the baseline nor the count holds it.
Under Codex no hook runs for a tool call, so only the rule applies.

Copilot reads the same hook files. The observer answers only when the result holds its output as text under the field names Claude Code uses, and reads no transcript under Copilot; Copilot's result shape and its delivery of context are unobserved.
While analysis or operator override is active the generated prelude answers in the hook's place, so nothing is detected or counted.

A printed line can only count when the parsed command roles or active syntax corroborate the named item. The final baseline with subagent threads has 28 commands with a shell-like line the classifier did not bear out. This is not a proof of perfect classification of arbitrary shell semantics.
A line a function of the command raised opens with the function's name and is not read, and neither is a line of another shell than zsh.
The transcript's shape and the hook's input are the host's, observed on Claude Code 2.1.284.

The count is local: it is removed with the worktree and a planning pass on main sees main's rows only. A lane that was removed holds no answers, so the failed results the transcript's last lines hold are answered once more.

Static reading is bounded to the command and literal nested scripts. Runtime function definitions, arbitrary computed values and dynamic shell state may not supply enough corroboration. No raw substring fallback is used to fill missing evidence.
routed: Registering the failed-command event (FUP-74e984d94ea97de5) would answer at the failed call itself. Its precondition is an observation of how Copilot treats that event in the registration file both hosts read, and WO-146 fixes that every Copilot launch is the operator's own.
